issues.description: The template Lecture class defines addGuestStudents with two parameters (int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), while the problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int) and the solution implements a single-parameter addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from implementing the method as specified by the exercise and expected by the solution/tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is desired as a pedagogical extension, either implement it inside the single-parameter method or provide an overloaded helper method (private or package-private) that includes validation, keeping the public API identical to the UML/problem statement.

issues.description: The template's addGuestStudents method signature does not match the problem specification and the solution. The problem statement and UML require addGuestStudents(int) (a single int parameter) while the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). This creates a mapping mismatch: students are instructed to implement a single-parameter method but the provided stub forces a different signature and an extra boolean parameter name (validateInput), which is not mentioned in the task or solution. This inconsistency will confuse students about the required method signature and expected usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by changing the template stub to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* ... */ }. If validation behavior is required, either implement it internally in that single-parameter method or provide an overloaded helper (e.g., private addGuestStudents(int, boolean) or a separate validate method) but keep the public API signature matching the specification.
